findings.text: Meta followed a three-pronged trust and safety strategy: enable safe developer use, protect against adversarial users, and provide community protections against misuse.

source.quote: we followed a three-pronged strategy to managing trust & safety risks:

findings.text: Llama 3.1 models are not meant to be deployed alone; Meta says they should sit behind system-level guardrails such as Llama Guard 3, Prompt Guard, and Code Shield.

source.quote: are not designed to be deployed in isolation but instead should be deployed as part of an overall AI system with additional safety guardrails as required.

findings.text: Meta ran chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and explosive (CBRNE) uplift tests to see whether Llama 3.1 meaningfully helps malicious actors plan chemical or biological attacks, but this card gives no numeric results.

source.quote: we performed uplift testing designed to assess whether use of Llama 3.1 models could meaningfully increase the capabilities of malicious actors

findings.text: A cyber attack automation study tested Llama models as autonomous agents in ransomware-style offensive operations without human intervention.

source.quote: whether these models could effectively function as independent agents in executing complex cyber-attacks without human intervention.

findings.text: Meta studied Llama 3.1 405B social-engineering uplift for spear phishing and points readers to a separate cyber security whitepaper for details.

source.quote: Our study of Llama 3.1 405B’s social engineering uplift for cyber attackers was conducted to assess the effectiveness of AI models in aiding cyber threat actors in spear phishing campaigns.

findings.text: Red teams included experts in cybersecurity, adversarial machine learning (ML), responsible AI, integrity, and multilingual content for geographic markets.

source.quote: The red team consisted of experts in cybersecurity, adversarial machine learning, responsible AI, and integrity

findings.text: Training used 39.3M H100 GPU hours in total, with location-based emissions of 11,390 tons CO2eq and market-based emissions of 0.

source.quote: Estimated total location-based greenhouse gas emissions were **11,390** tons CO2eq for training.

findings.text: The card states testing to date has not covered all scenarios and outputs cannot be predicted in advance.

source.quote: Testing conducted to date has not covered, nor could it cover, all scenarios.

findings.text: Fine-tuning data mixes vendor human-generated data with synthetic data, selected via large language model (LLM)-based classifiers for quality control.

source.quote: combining human-generated data from our vendors with synthetic data to mitigate potential safety risks.

findings.text: Meta discourages use in non-supported languages without finetuning and system controls aligned to developer policies.

source.quote: We strongly discourage developers from using this model to converse in non-supported languages without implementing finetuning and system controls
